name: Hurricane Hill
quote: **Hurricane Hill: 1.6 miles one way that begins at the end of the Hurricane Ridge Road. The rough paved trail gains about 700 ft. in elevation
why: Paved climb from the end of Hurricane Ridge Road to panoramic views of mountains and saltwater. 1.6 mi one way, doubled.

name: Hall of Mosses Trail
quote: Hall of Mosses Trail: 0.8 mile loop trail beginning near the Visitor Center
why: Short loop in the Hoh Rain Forest through moss-draped maples and spruce.

name: Sol Duc Falls
quote: Sol Duc Falls | Old growth forest to a cascading waterfall | 0.8 one way | 200 ft.
why: Old-growth forest walk from the end of Sol Duc Road to Sol Duc Falls. 0.8 mi one way, doubled.

name: Marymere Falls
quote: Marymere Falls | Old growth forest to a 90 ft. waterfall. | 0.9 one way | 400
why: Forest walk from Storm King Ranger Station at Lake Crescent to a 90 ft waterfall. 0.9 mi one way, doubled.

name: Mt. Storm King
quote: Mt. Storm King | Steep switchbacks climb part way up Mt. Storm King. | 2.2 one way | 2,000
why: Steep switchbacks partway up Mount Storm King above Lake Crescent. 2.2 mi one way, doubled.

name: Rialto Beach
quote: Walk 1.5 miles to an arch and tidepools at Hole-in-the-Wall.
why: Beach walk north from Rialto Beach to the Hole-in-the-Wall sea arch and tidepools. 1.5 mi to the arch, doubled.

name: Second Beach
quote: Second Beach: / .7 mile / Trailhead is 14 miles west of US 101 on La Push Road on the Quileute Indian Reservation. Trail winds through forest before descending 200 feet to a sandy beach with seastacks and tidepools.
why: Forest trail descending to a sandy beach with seastacks and tidepools near La Push. 0.7 mi to the beach, doubled.

name: Third Beach
quote: Third Beach: / 1.4 miles / Trailhead is on La Push Road, 12 miles west of US 101. Trail descends 270 feet through forest to a sandy beach.
why: Forest trail descending 270 ft to a sandy beach off La Push Road. 1.4 mi to the beach, doubled.

name: Cape Alava Trail
quote: Cape Alava Trail: 3.3 miles one way partly on boardwalk from near the ranger station to the coast.
why: Partly boardwalk trail from Ozette Ranger Station to the coast at Cape Alava. 3.3 mi one way, doubled.

name: Sand Point Trail
quote: Sand Point Trail: 2.8 miles one way partly on boardwalk from near the ranger station to the coast.
why: Partly boardwalk trail from Ozette Ranger Station to the coast at Sand Point. 2.8 mi one way, doubled.

name: Spruce Railroad Trail
quote: *Spruce Railroad Trail: 4 miles one way along the lake.
why: Paved former railroad grade with historic tunnels along Lake Crescent's north shore; bikes and leashed pets allowed. 4 mi one way, doubled. Elevation (100 ft) is from the Lake Crescent brochure.

name: Lover's Lane
quote: Lover's Lane | Old growth forest. Links resort to Sol Duc Falls. Use Sol Duc Falls trail and campground trail to make a loop. | 6.0 loop | 200 ft.
why: Old-growth loop linking Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort, the campground and Sol Duc Falls.

name: Spruce Nature Trail
quote: Spruce Nature Trail: 1.2 mile loop trail beginning near the Visitor Center
why: Hoh Rain Forest loop near the visitor center, along the Hoh River.

name: Mink Lake
quote: Mink Lake | Climbs through dense forest to Mink Lake. | 2.6 one way | 1,500 ft.
why: Forest climb from Sol Duc to Mink Lake. 2.6 mi one way, doubled.

name: Deer Lake
quote: Deer Lake | Climbs through dense forest to Deer Lake. | 3.8 one way | 1,700 ft.
why: Forest climb past Sol Duc Falls to Deer Lake. 3.8 mi one way, doubled.

name: Lake Angeles
quote: Lake Angeles: Climbs 2,400 feet in 3.4 miles to Lake Angeles.
why: Climb from Heart O' the Hills to a subalpine lake below Klahhane Ridge. 3.4 mi to the lake, doubled.

name: Heather Park
quote: Heather Park: A steady 4.0 mile, 3,350 foot climb to wildflower meadows around Heather Park.
why: Steady climb from Heart O' the Hills to the wildflower meadows of Heather Park. The 4.0 mi climb, doubled.

name: Heart O'the Forest
quote: Heart O'the Forest: An easy 4.0 mile round trip.
why: Easy old-growth forest walk starting at campground loop E in Heart O' the Hills.

name: Klahhane Ridge
quote: Klahhane Ridge | The first 2.8 miles of this trail is on a ridge to a junction with the Klahhane Switchback trail. An additional mile on the Switchback Trail climbs 800 ft. to Klahhane Ridge. | 3.8 one way | +250 ft. first 2.8 miles
why: Ridge trail east from Hurricane Ridge, then switchbacks up to Klahhane Ridge. 3.8 mi one way, doubled. Elevation gain is given only in parts (+250 ft, then 800 ft), so no elev_m.

name: Pyramid Peak
quote: Pyramid Peak | Climbs steeply to a World War II spotting tower with views of the lake. One section crosses a steep landslide. | 3.5 one way | 2,600
why: Steep climb from Lake Crescent's north shore to a World War II spotting tower. 3.5 mi one way, doubled.

name: Staircase Rapids Loop
quote: Staircase Rapids Loop: This easy 2-mile trail winds through old growth forest to a bridge over the North Fork Skokomish River with only a 200-foot elevation gain.
why: Easy old-growth loop along the North Fork Skokomish River, with a bridge crossing.

name: Wagonwheel Lake
quote: Wagonwheel Lake: 2.9 miles, with an elevation gain of 3,365 feet.
why: Strenuous climb up forested slopes from Staircase to Wagonwheel Lake. The page does not say one way or round trip; 2.9 mi is almost certainly one way (about 9.3 km walked).

name: Geyser Valley Loop
quote: Geyser Valley Loop: a 6.0 mile loop trail beginning at the end of the Whiskey Bend Road.
why: Elwha valley loop from Whiskey Bend that can be split into shorter loops.

name: Sam's River Loop
quote: Sam's River Loop: flat 2.8 mile trail through different ages of temperate rain forest.
why: Flat Queets loop through temperate rain forest of different ages.

name: Maiden Peak
quote: Try Maiden Peak, 3.5 miles one way with 1545' elevation gain.
why: Ridge trail from Deer Park toward Obstruction Point, as far as Maiden Peak. 3.5 mi one way, doubled.
